source_node.label: piSignage Arbitrary File Download via Path Traversal
source_node.precondition: Network access and authenticated low-privilege account on piSignage player API (version < 2.6.4).
source_node.postcondition: Arbitrary file disclosure on the Raspberry Pi host (including configuration files, shadow file, and logs) via api/settings/log?file=../.

target_node.label: Raspberry Pi Default Credential Exploitation
target_node.precondition: Network or local access to Raspberry Pi running Raspberry Pi OS (<= 5.10) with unchanged default credentials (pi:raspberry).
target_node.postcondition: Authenticated access to the system with 'pi' user privileges and access to sudo/administrative control.

offline.claim: Exfiltrated /etc/shadow or configuration files expose default 'pi' user credentials or system hashes

source.description: The web application component of piSignage before 2.6.4 allows a remote attacker (authenticated as a low-privilege user) to download arbitrary files from the Raspberry Pi via api/settings/log?file=../ path traversal. In other words, this issue is in the player API for log download.

applicability_rule.note: Arbitrary file read only; the record does not say what the files contain, so no foothold is granted.
applicability_rule.warning: E1 effect levels are not guaranteed CVE postconditions

source_node.label: Oculus Browser UI Injection and Code Execution
source_node.precondition: Target user visits a remote malicious web page using Oculus Browser (versions 5.2.7 through 5.7.11).
source_node.postcondition: Arbitrary HTML injection into browser UI, UI spoofing, and unprivileged code execution within the Oculus environment.

target_node.label: Oculus Desktop OVRRedir.exe Hard Link Arbitrary File Write
target_node.precondition: Unprivileged local code execution on Windows host running Oculus Desktop (< 1.44.0.32849).
target_node.postcondition: Privileged arbitrary file write via hard link to log file, leading to full Local Privilege Escalation (SYSTEM).

offline.claim: Initial code execution provides unprivileged local context on the host to create hard links to log files exploited by OVRRedir.exe

source.description: A remote web page could inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI, allowing an attacker to spoof UI and potentially execute code. This affects the Oculus Browser starting from version 5.2.7 until 5.7.11.

applicability_rule.note: 'potentially execute code': user-level foothold is the generous reading. Requires the victim to open an attacker-controlled page (inferred from 'remote web page').
applicability_rule.warning: E1 effect levels are not guaranteed CVE postconditions

target.description: Writing to an unprivileged file from a privileged OVRRedir.exe process in Oculus Desktop before 1.44.0.32849 on Windows allows local users to write to arbitrary files and consequently gain privileges via vectors involving a hard link to a log file.

applicability_rule.note: The CVE record's version field has a typo (1.44.0.328549); the description is used. 'gain privileges' is read as admin.
